00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:11.720: A sustained, resonant bell tone begins, low and clear, with a slow, natural decay. No speech, clicks, or volume jumps are present. The tone fills the audio space without interruption.

00:00:11.720 --> 00:00:13.000: The bell tone ends abruptly. A male voice begins speaking, clear and measured: “What is Nirvana?”

00:00:13.000 --> 00:00:28.000: The same male voice continues: “Nirvana is when everything the mind makes comes to a stop, the letting go of everything carried, the thirst ends, nothing pulls you anymore, stopping, going out, like a flame with no fuel. This is peaceful, this is excellent, namely the stilling of all preparations, the relinquishment of all assets, the destruction of craving, detachment, cessation, extinction.”

00:00:28.000 --> 00:00:29.000: A brief pause. No speech, no sound other than ambient silence.

00:00:29.000 --> 00:00:31.000: A different male voice begins: “Why don’t I see Nirvana right now?”

00:00:31.000 --> 00:00:54.000: The second male voice continues: “You do not see Nirvana right now, because you imagine a seer and a world, and neither is there. What is called ‘manana’ is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things. Only looking is there, nothing worth looking at. Only a seeing is there, nothing to be seen. The law of dependent arising is already implicated. There is therefore no seer apart from the phenomenon of seeing, according to the Tathagata.”

00:00:54.000 --> 00:00:55.000: A brief pause. No speech, no sound other than ambient silence.

00:00:55.000 --> 00:00:57.000: A third male voice begins: “What keeps it going?”

00:00:57.000 --> 00:01:09.000: The third male voice continues: “Thirst keeps it going, impelled by that making it into something, it runs towards the mirage, the gap is ignored. What impels one to ignore that gap is thirst. Perception. What impels one to ignore that gap is craving.”

00:05.000–00:06.000: Voice continues, same tone, no volume jump, no background noise. “What is called manana is the imagining in egoistic terms, imparting reality to illusory things.”

00:08.000–00:09.000: Voice continues, no pause. “Samsara is a whirlpool as far as the ordinary beings caught up in it are concerned.”

00:09.000–00:10.000: Voice continues, no change in pacing or tone. “Now what about the arhats? How is the idea of this whirlpool presented in the case of the arhats?”

00:10.000–00:11.000: Voice continues, no interruption. “It is simply said that for them, there is no whirling round, for there to be a designation.”

00:11.000–00:12.000: Voice continues, no change. “Pattantesa nati panna panaya. So in their case, there is no whirling round to justify a designation.”

00:12.000–00:13.000: Voice continues, no volume shift. “This then is something deeper than the whirlpool itself. The whirlpool can be pointed out because of its activity, but not so easily the emancipated ones.”

00:13.000–00:14.000: Voice continues, no change. “And that is why there is so much controversy.”

s6.text:
00:00.000–00:02.000: A sustained, high-pitched electronic tone, pure and steady, like a sine wave or test tone, fills the audio. No speech, no background noise.

00:02.000–00:03.000: The tone ends abruptly. Silence follows.

00:03.000–00:04.000: A male voice begins speaking, clear and natural, with no detectable synthetic quality. He says: “What is nirvana like?”

00:04.000–00:05.000: The same male voice continues: “Like a flame with no fuel.”

00:05.000–00:06.000: The voice continues: “I am grown cool, extinguished as I am.”

00:06.000–00:07.000: A different male voice begins, with a slightly different timbre, possibly a different recording or speaker. He says: “These preparations are comparable to a film.”

00:07.000–00:08.000: The second voice continues: “...which is the basic requirement for the film of name and form shown on the screen of consciousness of beings in this world.”

00:08.000–00:09.000: The second voice continues: “As the world is regarded as a sort of stage, trees, beings and objects in our environment are like objects on the stage.”

00:09.000–00:10.000: The second voice continues: “But the intriguing fact about it is that the ordinary man in the world is unaware of the prepared nature as a framework.”

00:10.000–00:11.000: The second voice continues: “When one is watching a film, one becomes unaware of the fact that it is just something shown on the screen.”

00:11.000–00:12.000: The second voice continues: “At that moment it appears as something real and lifelike.”
